subject: the Scaleway shapes a real fr-par account answered on a balancer and a public gateway (#434, #435)
why: Six changes, 90 of the 204 findings `feint corpus --check` reported once the acceptance entries naming #434 and #435 were stripped. Each was measured on corpus/scaleway/scw-billed-shapes.jsonl rather than argued from the SDK: a backend whose three optional defaults came back null instead of ""/false/false, a balancer that published no node at all, a list scoped to the pack's own project constant instead of the client's, a gateway address whose reverse was null where fr-par always answers a name, and a software version the emulator states as null in a shape the cloud never answers. The mutations below put each one back and require the test that names it to go red.

mutations.expect: a backend the client did not configure answers send_proxy_v2 and ssl_bridging null where fr-par answers false, on eleven operations at once
mutations.label: the absent booleans go back to null

mutations.expect: a backend answers host null where fr-par answers the empty string, so a client decoding it into a string gets a type it never sees on the real cloud
mutations.label: host goes back to null

mutations.expect: a balancer publishes no node, which is the shape 17 findings named through the eleven operations that nest a balancer
mutations.label: the balancer publishes no node

mutations.expect: the node's identifier is minted afresh on every read, which is the permanent Terraform diff a stable identity exists to prevent
mutations.label: the node identifier moves between two reads

mutations.expect: a list with no project filter is scoped to the pack's own constant, so a client that created an address under its own project gets an empty page from both lb and vpc-gw
mutations.label: a project-less list falls back to the pack's constant

mutations.expect: a freshly created gateway address answers reverse null where fr-par always answers a name, on the create, the read and the list at once
mutations.label: a gateway address goes back to a null reverse

mutations.expect: clearing a reverse writes null back into the store, so a client that empties the name gets a type the cloud never answers
mutations.label: clearing a reverse restores the null

mutations.expect: the gateway states 'no version' as a null key, which is a type divergence no field decline can reach — the decline reads as covering it and covers nothing
mutations.label: the version comes back as a null key
